newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish mostly lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished mostly lower in a session dominated by technical weakness and post-Greenspan jitters.

Wednesday's comments from Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan continued to haunt the market on Thursday, as worries of an imminent rate hike continued. Thursday afternoon comments from Federal Reserve vice chairwoman Alice Rivlin further spooked players.
"With Greenspan Wednesday and also from these Rivlin comments as well, they may be setting themselves for a possible move in March," one T-bond futures trader said.
The next Federal Open Market Committee meeting is March 25. Greenspan delivers his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony next week to the House Banking Committee.

Greenspan told the Senate on Wednesday that the U.S. stock market's rise might be "unsustainable" and said he saw more upside inflation risks. He added he would not rule out a pre-emptive credit tightening to ward off inflation.
"Greenspan just scared the hell out of the market," one Eurodollar broker said, adding that weakness could permeate Friday as well.
Rivlin repeated her view on the U.S. eocnomy late Thursday, saying its biggest threat would be "too much of a good thing."
Rivlin said the Fed was carefully watching for any signs of increasing inflation.
March T-bonds and June and September Eurodollars all fell through Wednesday's session lows in afternoon trading, a condition that points to more weakness Friday, several traders said.
"Keep an eye on the inflation component of the GDP revision tomorrow," the Euro trader said.
Others said signs of strength in any of the data due on Friday could again raise the rate-hike specter.

On Friday, fourth-quarter revised real gross domestic product will be released, then January existing home sales, Chicago purchasing managers' data and the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index.
June Treasury bond futures will become the lead T-bond futures contract beginning in Thursday's night open-outcry trading session.
Traders pegged near-term support at 110-1/32, the 200-day moving average, and at 109-14/32, the January low.

At the close, March T-bonds were down 4/32 points at 110-24/32, 10-year notes fell 4/32 to 108-08/32, munis gained 1/32 to 115-26/32, June T-bills fell two basis points to 94.78, and June Eurodollars fell three to 94.22. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
